title: Incident declare modal: add taxonomy v1 fields + validation + unit tests
author: Devon Price
description: Context: As part of the “Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping” reliability initiative, we’re standardizing incident categorization at declaration time so we can (a) route pages correctly and (b) compute MTTR/TTM by category/owner without post-hoc cleanup. This PR updates the Slack incident declaration flow (modal) to collect taxonomy v1 metadata with lightweight defaults and strict allowed-values validation. What’s included: 1) Slack modal updates (/incident declare and the interactive “Declare incident” action) - Adds new fields: Incident category (required), Impacted surface (required), Customer tier (required), Region (required), Impact summary (required, existing), Impact start time (optional, existing), Contributing factors (optional multi-select), Notes/internal context (optional). - Field order is optimized for lowest cognitive load during active response (category/surface/tier/region first; contributing factors optional). 2) Defaults - Customer tier defaults to “Unknown” (must be changed if known; see validation below). - Region defaults to “Unknown” unless the declare command is invoked in a region-scoped channel (we currently infer from channel naming convention: #incidents-us-east-1, #incidents-eu-west-1). - Impacted surface defaults to “Hosted API” unless “dedicated” appears in the channel name/topic (best-effort only). 3) Allowed values + validation - Adds a versioned taxonomy config (taxonomies/taxonomy_v1.json) with allowed values for category/surface/tier/region/contributing_factors. - Enforces required fields at submit time (Slack modal submission). - Enforces allowed values on every categorical field (rejects unknown/stale values; returns a user-facing error message prompting re-open of the modal). - Adds a guardrail for “Unknown”: tier and region may remain Unknown at declaration time, but if the incident is marked Sev1 or Sev2 in the modal, we prompt the user to confirm they truly don’t know (Slack modal error + hint). We’re intentionally not blocking declare on Unknown to avoid slowing response, but we do make it harder to accidentally skip. 4) Persistence payload changes - Updates the incident record schema written to incident-store to include: taxonomy_version, category, impacted_surface, customer_tier, region, contributing_factors. - The new fields are additive and default to null/Unknown when older clients submit records (backward compatible for existing incidents). 5) Unit tests - Adds tests for modal construction (fields present, required flags set, default behavior). - Adds tests for validation rules (required fields, allowed values, Unknown confirmations for Sev1/Sev2). - Adds snapshot tests for the Slack view payload (kept small; we strip volatile view IDs). Out of scope (follow-ups): - Ownership auto-suggestion based on category/impacted service (tracked separately; see PR #223). - Server-side migration/backfill of historical incidents (ENG-4826). - Dashboard wiring (observability pipeline) lives in slo-toolkit/observability-pack workstreams. Rollout plan: - Behind feature flag TAXONOMY_V1_FIELDS (default off). - Enable in #incidents-sandbox for 1 day; then enable for all eng-oncall workspaces. - If we need rollback: disable the flag (no schema rollback required; fields are additive). Screenshots: - Added in the PR attachments (before/after modal) and in docs/incident-bot-taxonomy.md. Notes for Support/CS: - The new metadata is posted into the incident channel’s pinned “Incident details” message so Support can quickly see tier/region/category without asking IC. Testing: - Unit tests: yarn test - Integration smoke: ran locally with ngrok + Slack dev workspace; verified validation messages render correctly and record is persisted with taxonomy fields. Related: ENG-4824, ENG-4822, ENG-4829, INT-330.
commits: modal: add taxonomy v1 fields to declare flow
validation: enforce allowed values + required fields on submit
storage: persist taxonomy fields onto incident record
tests: modal payload snapshot + validation cases
docs: update incident-bot usage notes for taxonomy fields
review_conversation: Miles Thornton: Can we keep the category list short in the modal and rely on postmortems for granularity? Author: Agree. This PR uses the v1 “top-level” categories only (no subtypes). Contributing factors stays optional and can be refined later.

Allison Grant: Please ensure values are versioned; dashboards will join on taxonomy_version. Author: Added taxonomy_version: "v1" persisted with incident record; loader reads from taxonomies/taxonomy_v1.json.

Rafael Mendes: Validation should not block incident declaration if region/tier is unknown; on-call won’t always know. Author: Implemented non-blocking for Unknown, but adds confirmation warning for Sev1/Sev2 to reduce accidental skips.

Dev Patel: Support needs region + tier visible without digging; can we surface in the pinned summary. Author: Updated the channel “Incident details” message template to include category/surface/tier/region and contributing factors when present.
Rafael Mendes (follow-up): Please add a migration note for older incidents that won’t have these fields. Author: Added backward-compat handling in incidentRecord parsing + doc note.
release_notes: Incident declaration modal now collects taxonomy v1 metadata (category, impacted surface, customer tier, region, contributing factors).
Validation enforces required fields and allowed values; Unknown tier/region allowed with guardrails for high-severity incidents.
